title: Lift a residue automorphism through a strict henselization to a fraction-field separable closure
statement: Let $(H,\mathfrak m_H,\kappa)$ be a henselian normal local domain [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], put $F=\operatorname{Frac}(H)$, and choose a separable closure $\kappa_s/\kappa$ [def-pd-separable-closure]. Let $R$ be the strict henselization of $H$ at this residue closure [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with $R/\mathfrak m_R=\kappa_s$. Suppose $R$ is a domain and an $H$-embedding $R\hookrightarrow\Omega$ into a separable closure $\Omega/F$ is given. Then for every $\tau\in\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa_s/\kappa)$ there exist an $H$-algebra automorphism $t:R\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ reducing to $\tau$, its extension $t_L:\operatorname{Frac}(R)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ over $F$, and an automorphism $u\in\operatorname{Aut}_F(\Omega)$ restricting to $t_L$. More precisely, if $B_e$ are finite local etale $H$-algebras with residue $e$ whose filtered colimit over finite Galois subextensions $e/\kappa$ of $\kappa_s/\kappa$ is identified with $R$ [lem-wf-strict-henselization-finite-lifts], there are unique $H$-automorphisms $t_e$ of $B_e$ reducing to $\tau|_e$, they commute with every transition $B_e\to B_f$, and their induced colimit automorphism is $t$.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, lemma-identify-inertia, paragraph on automorphisms of the strict henselization; algebra.tex Tag 0BSL, remark-construct-sh-from-h, and Tag 04GK, lemma-henselian-cat-finite-etale.

proof.text: Use H itself as its henselization: the identity local map H\to H has the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], since a factorization of any local map g:H\to T through the identity must be g. Apply [lem-wf-strict-henselization-finite-lifts] with A=H. It supplies the finite local etale lifts B_e and identifies their colimit, restricted to finite Galois intermediate fields e/\kappa of \kappa_s, with R, respecting H and the residue maps. Write i_e:B_e\to R and q_e:B_e\to e for the coprojections and residue maps. This also applies to any diagram and residue-compatible colimit identification specified in the last clause of the item; the argument below uses only those data.

Fix \tau\in\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa_s/\kappa). Each finite Galois e/\kappa is preserved by \tau. Indeed for x\in e, the minimal polynomial of x over \kappa splits in e; \tau(x) is a root of that same polynomial, so lies in e. The same argument for \tau^{-1} gives \tau(e)=e. Thus \tau_e=\tau|_e is a \kappa-automorphism, and for e\subset f the two maps e\to f given by \tau_f followed after inclusion and inclusion followed after \tau_e agree elementwise. Here normality is part of the finite Galois condition stated in [lem-wf-strict-henselization-finite-lifts].

source.place: Tag 0BSW, lemma-identify-inertia, proof paragraph identifying automorphisms of the strict henselization with residue Galois automorphisms.

proof.text: Apply the Hom-set bijection [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-map-bijective] over the henselian local base H to S=T=B_e. It lifts \tau_e uniquely to an H-map t_e:B_e\to B_e. Lift \tau_e^{-1} to s_e by the same bijection. Both s_et_e and t_es_e reduce to the identity, so injectivity of this bijection gives s_et_e=t_es_e=\mathrm{id}; hence t_e is an automorphism. For a transition v_{ef}:B_e\to B_f, the maps t_fv_{ef} and v_{ef}t_e have the same reduction by step 2, so the same bijection, now with S=B_e,T=B_f, makes them equal. The inverse maps s_e satisfy the identical compatibility. All applications have finite etale source and target; no claim about Hom into an infinite colimit is being made.

The compatible maps i_et_e induce an H-endomorphism t of R by the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; the compatible i_es_e induce s. On every coprojection, sti_e=i_es_et_e=i_e and tsi_e=i_et_es_e=i_e. Uniqueness in that universal property gives st=ts=\mathrm{id}. Let q:R\to\kappa_s be the specified residue quotient. The residue-compatible identification in [lem-wf-strict-henselization-finite-lifts] gives qt i_e=\operatorname{incl}_e q_et_e=\operatorname{incl}_e\tau_eq_e=\tau qi_e for every e. The same colimit uniqueness, with target \kappa_s, gives qt=\tau q. Therefore the induced residue automorphism of t is \tau, and its restrictions on the finite-stage coprojections are exactly the required t_e.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, lemma-identify-inertia, proof paragraph identifying automorphisms of the strict henselization with residue Galois automorphisms.

proof.text: Put L=\operatorname{Frac}(R). Define t_L(a/b)=t(a)/t(b) for a,b\in R, b\ne0. The denominator is nonzero since t is injective. The relation a/b=c/d is ad=cb, which t preserves, so the formula is well defined; the usual common-denominator addition and multiplication identities show it is a field homomorphism. The same formula for s is its inverse. Since t fixes H, this map fixes all fractions from H, hence F. The given embedding j:R\hookrightarrow\Omega extends by j_L(a/b)=j(a)/j(b); the same fraction identities show it is a field embedding fixing F. Identify L with its image under j_L.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, lemma-identify-inertia, proof paragraph identifying automorphisms of the strict henselization with residue Galois automorphisms.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois](2), the given separable closure \Omega/F is algebraic and normal (take the intermediate base field to be F). Apply [lem-sfb-normal-intermediate-isomorphism-lifts] with k=F, ambient field \Omega, both intermediate subfields equal to j_L(L), and intermediate isomorphism j_Lt_Lj_L^{-1}. Its hypotheses require normality only of \Omega/F, not of L/F. It gives u\in\operatorname{Aut}_F(\Omega) satisfying uj_L=j_Lt_L. This is the asserted extension, and steps 3 and 4 give all the finite-stage uniqueness and compatibility clauses.
